Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>

Subject: Zenith Health — Renewal & Capacity Coordination

Hi Emma / Zenith procurement team —

Thanks again for the ongoing partnership. Your current subscription is up for renewal in late October and I wanted to kick off the renewal + capacity conversation so we can avoid any last-minute friction. High-level goals for this thread:

- Confirm term length and price cadence for renewal (we've prepared a 12-mo and 18-mo proposal)
- Align on capacity uplift needed (customer engineering requested ~30% throughput uplift)
- Schedule a technical pre-brief and the renewal QBR so stakeholders are present
- Circulate a mutual action plan (MAP) and target contract timeline

Proposed timeline (flexible):
- Sept 15: Technical pre-brief (30 min) — infra + solutions engineer
- Sept 22: Renewal QBR (60 min) — exec + procurement + SRE
- Oct 05: Finalize commercial terms and send to legal
- Oct 20: Contract signed / effective date starting Nov 1

I've attached an initial MAP and the SLA proposal for your review (see attachments). Marcus has outlined capacity options below; Marcus / Monica — can you attach the uplift workbook and a quick delta on committed vs burst pricing?

Emma — can you confirm the best procurement contact and the lead for infrastructure so we can send calendar invites? If Sept 22 works, we'll hold a 11:00am ET slot and circulate an invite.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_v1.xlsx, SLA-proposal.pdf

Next steps:
1) Emma to confirm stakeholders + preferred QBR window
2) Marcus to share capacity uplift options and associated cost deltas
3) I will draft the term options and send a redline-ready agreement after the QBR

Thanks — looking forward to getting this scheduled and keeping things smooth.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Hi all —

Attaching the capacity uplift workbook (capacity_uplift_options.xlsx) and a short summary below. Happy to walk through on the Sept 15 pre-brief.

Short summary:
- Option A (staircase): +30% committed throughput via staged dedicated capacity. Delta: +$18,500/mo relative to current committed tier. 12-mo term shown; 18-mo reduces delta by ~12%.
- Option B (burst + cache tuning): achieve ~20-25% effective uplift without committed capacity; lower cost but higher variance on peak days. Suitable if you want minimal contract changes.
- Option C (hybrid): +15% dedicated + burst buffer — recommended if you need a safety valve during campaigns. Delta: +$10,200/mo.

Attachments include per-region breakdown, expected latency SLO impact, and a sample amendment that lists commit changes.

Emma — for the SOW ask, the sample amendment is in the workbook under the "Legal" tab; Vivek will draft an initial commercial summary after QBR and we can feed that to legal.

I'll hold Sept 15 mornings ET open for a 30-min tech check with Liam and his team.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
